source.anchor_kjv: And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and much people. Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her. And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not. And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise. And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother. And there came a fear on all: and they glorified God, saying, That a great prophet is risen up among us; and, That God hath visited his people. And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judaea, and throughout all the region round about.
source.hook_line: A widow was walking behind her only son's body, carried out on a bier to be buried.
source.spoken_script: A widow was walking behind her only son's body, carried out on a bier to be buried. He was all she had left. The law was simple: touch a dead man, and you were unclean. Everyone kept their distance. That was survival, not cruelty. Jesus walked toward her instead of away. And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, "Weep not." Then he touched what no one else would touch: and he came and touched the bier, and they that bare him stood still. Under that same law, the touch should have made him unclean. It didn't work that way with him. And he said, "Young man, I say unto thee, Arise." And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother. Death didn't spread from the boy to Jesus. Life spread from Jesus to the boy. That is still the only direction he touches anything dead in you. Not to catch what's wrong with you — to give you what's his instead. He touched a funeral, and it became a homecoming.

platforms.title: He Touched a Dead Man's Bier, and the Funeral Became a Homecoming
platforms.description:
Luke 7:11-17: Jesus and his disciples came to the gate of the city of Nain just as a funeral was going out. A widow was burying her only son. Under the law, touching a dead body made a person ceremonially unclean, so the crowd kept its distance. That was survival, not cruelty.

"And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not."

Then he did what no one else in the procession would do. "And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still." "Young man, I say unto thee, Arise."

"And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother."

Under that same law, the touch should have made Jesus unclean. It did not work that way with him. Death did not spread from the boy to Jesus. Life spread from Jesus to the boy.

That is still the only direction he moves toward anything dead in you. Not to catch what is wrong with you, but to give you what is his instead.

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS

- Every quoted fragment ("Weep not", "touched the bier... stood still", "Young man, I say unto thee, Arise", "sat up, and began to speak... delivered him to his mother") checked against the given Luke 7:11-17 text - all exact, continuous, no elisions.
- "Under that same law, the touch should have made Jesus unclean" is a doctrinally careful way to state the reversal (the text implies it via the ceremonial-uncleanness law, and the narration itself frames it this way) - not an invented claim.
- No fear/gain-loss framing; "not to catch what is wrong with you, but to give you what is his instead" is grace-anchored, consistent across all five platforms.
- Titles are honest and specific to the actual scene (a funeral procession physically interrupted), not generic "amazing miracle" clickbait language.
- TikTok/Instagram front-load the concrete stakes (burying an only son, the touch being taboo) in the first line; YouTube/Facebook carry the full quoted sequence. No platform mismatch.
